Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-08-31 | AMZN | Underweight | -1.1% | -0.9% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN stays Underweight: trim roughly half of a full single-name position to a ~50% residual (working range 45–55%), executed in two buckets — 25–30% of the trim ratably over the next three to five sessions with limit orders near market, and the balance at $261.54 (10-EMA), $265.67 (20-SMA) and $272.00 (mid-gap). Resolve the plan's contradiction: a close above $272.65 on ≥40M shares cancels the $272.00 tranche and forces reassessment instead of a sell-then-rebuy inside a two-dollar band. Treat $252 as a slippage-prone decision level rather than a stop (the untraded gap runs $239.82–$262.01 and the 50-SMA shelf sits inside it), cut toward 25–30% of standard weight on a close below, exit the residual below $239.82, and hold at target weight before the late-October Q3 print. No new long until a volume reclaim of $272.00–$272.65 or a weekly close above $280; no short at $259.77.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction is not close; execution and size are. Every seat and the Research Manager converges on reducing AMZN, and the aggressive analyst is right that here the aggressive action and the prudent action are the same trade. The bear file carries four unrepaired items. Earnings quality: the $50.5B non-cash mark-up was ~62% of Q2 pre-tax income ($62.8B / ~52% in H1), leaving core EPS near $2.16 against a $5.75 headline — a mid-30s multiple on clean earnings with H1 FCF of −$27B, TTM −$11.6B, no buyback and no dividend. Forward cost: capex at 2.71× D&A with D&A already 10% of revenue and growing +31.3% YoY faster than revenue means current margins are flattered by assets whose depreciation has not landed; the bull's "earnings power hasn't been reflected" runs backwards. Margin quality: 225bp of the 226bp comes from SBC (−89bp), marketing (−98bp) and G&A (−38bp), with SBC at 3.01% of revenue near the mega-cap floor and the marketing cut taken into escalating Temu/Shein/Walmart/Microsoft/Google spend. Cash accounting: $3.98B of cash taxes on $120.7B pre-tax (3.3% vs 23% book) with $41.4B TTM deferred tax means OCF and FCF are subsidised, not conservative. On the $650B of obligations the Research Manager's reversal is decisive and unrebutted — they are Amazon's commitments to pay, a fixed cost — and there is no AWS backlog or customer-commitment figure anywhere in the supplied dataset, a gap to flag to the desk rather than fill with an assumed demand tail.\n\nThe tape argues the same way at lower conviction and is used for sizing and entry, not for the thesis. Price at $259.77 is 8.8% above a rising 200-SMA (238.73) and 3.1% above a 50-SMA that turned up off 246.38, so the primary trend is intact — hence a trim, not an exit or a short, consistent with the record that heavy AMZN de-risking inside a rising structure repeatedly forfeited alpha. But price has closed below the 10-EMA (261.54) in 12 of 13 sessions and below the VWMA (262.05) where every recent buyer is underwater, MACD has sat below signal for eleven sessions, and upside to the $272.00–$272.65 shelf is +5.0% against −7.7% through air to $239.82. The bull plan itself saying "do not buy $259–$262" while the stock closed at $259.77 is the tell: hold-with-overlay, not accumulate.\n\nI side with the neutral and conservative on execution because the aggressive's \"convex\" label does not survive the order book: with 80% of the reduction queued above spot, the bear's own base case — a fade from here — produces no fills and carries full exposure into the event being de-risked. So a ratable near-market bucket is mandatory and the $272.00-sell versus $272.65-halt contradiction must be resolved before orders go in. I also accept that $252 is not a stop: the untraded range is $239.82–$262.01, price has already re-entered it, and the $251.97/$252.35 shelf sits inside the vacuum, so realised fills on that branch are mid-$240s to $250 — size, not the trigger, is the protection. Conversely I reject the conservative's 40% cap, since his own concessions (+$43.9B net cash ex-leases, ~21x coverage, operating income +43.2%, OCF +44%) make a punitive floor over-correction; 50% residual with a $252-driven step to 25–30% and a $239.82 exit is the right middle. I equally refuse to hang timing on the aggressive's \"60–70% YoY EPS decline\" — the Q3-2025 base is not in this dataset and H1-2025 non-operating income was only ~$4.96B — or on the tripled Nvidia GPU headline, which is two-sided and secondarily sourced with no primary filing. The mark-up cliff is still a real dated risk, so be at target weight before the late-October print, but it is not a forecast.\n\nUpgrade to Overweight on two of: capex-to-OCF converging from 1.38x toward 1.0x and capex/D&A rolling down from 2.71x over two visible quarters; D&A/revenue stabilising with gross margin holding; TTM FCF turning positive; disclosure of a genuine AWS backlog or AI-revenue figure; or a transaction validating the $122.3B model-valued book. Downgrade to Sell on a close below $252 that fails to reclaim within two to three sessions, a break of $239.82, or any markdown/flat-mark quarter on that book. Unverified and not underwritten: no AWS segment revenue, margin or backlog in the dataset; no identity or valuation inputs for the $122.3B stake; no Q3-2025 comparative base; incomplete news and no usable insider data; no portfolio or cash context, so all sizing is a fraction of a caller-defined standard AMZN weight.

**Price Target**: 250.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print

REFLECTION:
Overweight/underweight ask was answered by the tape, not the fundamentals: AMZN returned -1.1% raw and -0.9% alpha versus SPY over the five days, the right sign for an Underweight, though five sessions against a 1–3 month, Q3-print-anchored thesis is too short to score the call itself. What the window does support is the tactical layer — price stayed pinned below the 10-EMA and VWMA with every recent buyer underwater, exactly the "hold-with-overlay, not accumulate" read, and neither the $252 step-down nor the $272.65 cancel level was touched, so the sizing plan ran untested rather than validated. The core thesis (earnings-quality mark-up, capex/D&A at 2.71x, tax subsidy of FCF) remains entirely unscored by price and stays open until the late-October print. Lesson for next time: keep the ratable near-market bucket as the majority of execution and treat above-spot tranches as optionality, since the base case here produced no fills and the residual carried full exposure.

[2026-08-28 | AMZN | Underweight | -3.0% | -3.1% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AMZN: trim roughly half of the existing position (benchmark 100 units → ~50 units) at market near 266.43, keeping a real core rather than exiting, and apply the same proportional cut if the caller sits above or below a standard allocation. Stage the residual behind two levels: a daily close below 255.02 halves what remains, and a daily close below 251.5 (50-SMA 251.66 and lower Bollinger 251.56, ~0.10 apart) takes it to token/zero because the unfilled 235.50–262.01 gap void opens beneath. Put on no tactical long at spot; the only permitted add is 10–15% of a standard allocation on a single defined trigger — a 262–263 retest holding on declining volume with a stop below 255.02, or a close above 267.56 on ≥40M shares with the MACD histogram turning positive, not both — with total AMZN exposure capped near 60% of standard until the 272–274 supply shelf clears. Do not short; horizon 3–6 months, re-scored on the Q3 10-Q.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats converged on reducing AMZN and none defended a full position, so the decision turns on size, on whether the tactical-long sleeve belongs, and on which version of the bear case to trust. The direction wins on arithmetic rather than rhetoric: the bullish file's load-bearing fact is inverted. The $650.0B of contractual obligations is money Amazon owes — $78.1B due inside twelve months plus $116.4B of undiscounted operating leases — while the only disclosed revenue-visibility line, deferred revenue, is $24.9B and flat YoY ($20,428M vs $20,576M); the "2.1x covered by CFO" claim fails because that $161.4B of CFO is the same cash already committed to $173.0B of TTM capex. Cash conversion is unambiguous and uncontested by any seat: Q2 CFO $45.4B against capex $54.2B (119% capex-to-CFO); H1 CFO $71.4B against $98.4B of capex plus $39.8B of acquisitions, a $66.8B hole plugged with $62.9B of financing; TTM FCF −$11.6B versus +$13.5B a year earlier; ~$65B of gross debt added in six months; interest expense +155% YoY; $106.1B of balance-sheet expansion from Level-3 marks; $30.5B of H1 deferred tax expense against $4.0B of cash taxes paid. On the bull's own concession (~$1.95 Q2 normalized, ~$7.90–8.20 annualized) that is ~33x normalized earnings while consuming cash, with no buyback and no dividend. The margin bridge reads as borrowed, not structural: of ~226bp of Q2 operating-margin expansion, 98bp came from marketing growing +2.5% against +19.6% revenue and 38bp from G&A falling 6.0% in absolute dollars — roughly 60% from levers that can only be pulled once or twice — while D&A is already 9.97% of revenue (+89bp YoY) against the $173.0B TTM capex that has not yet depreciated, so the bulk of the charge is still ahead. The tape corroborates timing but not liquidation: close 266.43 under the 266.88 Bollinger middle and under the plan's own 267.56 trigger, on 49.55M shares versus the 129.05M/90.83M sessions that built overhead supply, MACD 2.086 below its 3.200 signal (histogram −1.114), and the 287.20 → 280.14 → 266.40 → 267.56 lower-high sequence intact. Weighing the seats: the aggressive analyst is right that waiting on confirmation has a cost, but a 60% core plus a 25% tactical long is up to 85% gross exposure to the same unresolved risk, and he demands confirmation above 267.56 while pre-positioning a long below it — the neutral's objection, which is decisive. The conservative analyst is right that negative FCF, a Level-3 earnings mark and a levered balance sheet justify more than a 40% trim and right to delete the pre-confirmation long, but a 60–70% cut leaving 30–40% with no optionality over-de-risks a name whose primary structure has not broken, and the record shows heavy AMZN Underweights and near-exits inside an intact rising 50/200-SMA structure (07-22 through 07-30) cost +12% to +22% of five-day alpha while the measured 08-12 trim was roughly neutral. The neutral's calibration wins: trim about half, treat 255.02 as an intermediate trigger rather than a thesis break (only ~1.6 ATR below spot, inside the noise band — the conservative's near-final exit level would whipsaw), reserve 251.5 as the true invalidation, replace the 25% sleeve with a 10–15% gated one, and cap total exposure until 272–274 clears. Rating is Underweight rather than Sell because the business case is intact — revenue accelerated to +19.6% from +16.6%, operating income +43.2% to $27.5B on a 13.69% margin with a third consecutive quarter of expansion, inventory −0.4% on +19.6% revenue, $176.1B of cash and securities, net cash positive on the narrow definition, and price 5.9% above a rising 50-SMA and 11.6% above a rising 200-SMA (238.68). What would change the call: upward on MACD histogram turning positive with a daily close above 274.5 on ≥40M shares, or a 251.5–255.0 flush holding on declining volume with MACD improving, plus at least three Q3 10-Q scorecard items — sequential capex below Q2's $54.2B, deferred revenue inflecting off $24.9B, EquitySecuritiesWithoutReadilyDeterminableFairValueAmount holding at or above $122.3B (a first downward mark is thesis-breaking and triggers an immediate further cut), no repeat of the $67.0B H1 long-term debt raise, and marketing as a percentage of revenue stabilizing while margins still expand. Downward on a daily close below 251.5, or a 10-Q showing capex-to-revenue still rising, total debt above ~$150B, or any markdown in the equity-stake book. Explicit gaps that cap conviction both ways: no sentiment/positioning data and no insider transaction data in this run — so the aggressive analyst's "marginal buyer exhaustion" is asserted on a dataset with no positioning information; no AWS segment revenue, margin or backlog, leaving the demand side of the $173B capex program unverified; no identity or valuation inputs for the $122.3B Level-3 book; and no portfolio, holdings or cash context, so all sizing is expressed as fractions of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation.

**Price Target**: 252.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the Q3 10-Q

REFLECTION:
The 5-day window delivered −3.1% alpha against SPY, so the Underweight call was directionally correct — AMZN fell 3.0% while the benchmark held — though five days tests only the entry timing, not the cash-conversion and Level-3-mark thesis that the 3–6 month horizon and Q3 10-Q re-score are built on. What the window supports is the tape half of the thesis: the close at 266.43 below the 266.88 Bollinger middle, MACD 2.086 under its 3.200 signal, and the intact 287.20 → 267.56 lower-high sequence all resolved downward as read, and deleting the pre-confirmation tactical long was right since the 262–263 and 267.56 triggers never printed. It undercuts nothing on the fundamental side but leaves the 255.02 intermediate trigger untested (price near 258.4, only ~1.6 ATR below entry), so next time I would size the initial trim closer to the full intended reduction when the tape corroborates but structure is intact, rather than parking half the decision behind a confirmation level that may not print inside the review window.

[2026-08-27 | AMZN | Overweight | +1.0% | +0.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Overweight, built in stages rather than bought whole at 256.26: take a 20–25% starter of a ~1.0–1.25x standard target now, add ~25–30% only if the 251.08–252 confluence holds on a reversal candle with volume under ~30M, and split the remainder above a close of 260.93 on >40M shares and then above 264.11 (VWMA) toward 267.14. Hard invalidation 246.50, cut to half-size on any daily close below 251.08, and no new capital in the 248.57→235.50 air pocket. Size the starter off a stress gap toward 238.59/235.50, not just the 9.76-point stop, because the 1% risk claim in the plan is arithmetically wrong at a 40% first tranche. Horizon 3–6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction goes to the aggressive analyst; size, entry and add discipline go to the neutral analyst — the same split the Research Manager reached, and the neutral's arithmetic correction is the one point in the debate nobody rebutted.

What the aggressive proved and the conservative never overturned: revenue growth accelerated 16.6%→19.6% on a ~$200B quarterly base; operating income +43.2% to $27.46B at a 13.7% margin (+230bp) through a 31–42% rise in depreciation; marketing +2.5%, G&A −6.0%, SBC −7.6% against 19.6% revenue growth; core EPS (ex-marks) ~+26%; net debt/EBITDA ~0.37x with $176.1B liquidity and ~21x coverage. Structure: higher lows 199.14→225.55→226.16, higher highs 264.50→278.56→287.20, price 7.4% above a rising 200 SMA (238.59), 50 SMA up 20 straight sessions to 251.08, pullback on ~65% of normal volume. This corrects my own record: four AMZN Underweights (08-14 to 08-20) captured only +1.5%, −0.2%, −1.5% and −2.6% of five-day alpha, and the 08-20 review found over-de-risking an intact primary trend to be the recurring error; the 08-18 Overweight (+0.8% alpha) taught that the failure mode is parking a constructive rating while price sits 5–12% above its 10 EMA. At 256.26 AMZN is below the 10 EMA (260.93) and VWMA (264.11), on the 50% retracement (255.34) of the 226.65→284.02 impulse — the entry geometry I have been waiting for, not the one I was warned about.

The conservative wins on risk composition and I carry it in full. At ~$7.80 annualized core EPS the stock is ~33x with TTM FCF −$11.6B and H1 FCF −$27.0B; capex 27% of revenue (~$54.2B in Q2) against ~$80B annualized D&A, so the depreciation bill is still ahead; debt +93% to $133.0B in six months; interest expense +155% with net interest flipping from +$569M to −$19M; current ratio 1.03x; $650B contractual obligations ($78.1B due inside twelve months) plus $109.8B lease obligations. Earnings quality is the largest unhedged risk: 81% of Q2 net income ($50.5B of $62.6B) is a non-cash markup of non-marketable equity that grew that book from $16.2B to $122.3B — 11.2% of assets, self-marked, no observable price, no disclosed identity or inputs; a markdown arrives as a gap, and the July 31 +12.5% session proves this name gaps double digits. The AWS–NVIDIA headline is a commitment, not revenue (two million GPUs in 2027–28, no dollar value, financing, exclusivity or incrementality), and the 08-27 tape confirmed the timing objection: AMZN closed −1.54% on 35.9M vs 21.5M shares in the bottom third of the range after a midday catalyst.

The conservative overreaches only at the prescription. His case is about price, entry timing and earnings composition, not deterioration of the operating engine, and his own framing is a staging instruction.
